structuralConstraint: Use the production maximum of 256 tokens for upper structural blocks in the primary comparison. Repeat selection allowing larger structural cores as a separate stress test while holding the final passage to 512 tokens. Tune the two-structural-layout control independently in both regimes.
optionalKeys: Before opening validation results, on the frozen compact geometries also retest the cosine of a normalized mixture of neighboring paragraph vectors, individual sentence keys, consecutive triples, and triples gated at cosine 0.25. Tune the detail share and the contribution of the small keys on development. Compare these separately with the independently selected extended blocks index and record the distinct serving vectors.
selection: Use only the seven-domain development pool to nominate each family. Independently retune structural and semantic layouts. Select by the equal-weight mean of complete evidence first and within five. Within 0.35 percentage points of the highest mean, prefer the simpler scoring method and then the higher first-hit citation F1. Keep the 512-token displayed ceiling. Use the same ranking controls for the single layouts and compare two structural layouts as a control for indexing two segmentations. Take shortlisted geometries through paragraph/section weighting, paragraph neighbor scoring and duplicate suppression. Freeze nominees before reading their validation scores.
paragraphNeighbors: For a contained paragraph occurrence, blend the question-to-paragraph score with the mean or maximum question cosine to its immediately adjacent paragraphs. Test within the same source section or record, and allow crossing authored sections as a control. Test neighbors present in the displayed window and a fresh embedding of the scoped three-paragraph text. Allow a coextensive paragraph when it is the whole core. Independently test an enclosing paragraph of at most 512 tokens as a fallback for split fragments. Neither the returned window nor its evidence is expanded by these ranking trials.
topFive: Compare score-sorted union, a joint first hit followed by structural hits, reranking the same five structural hits with overlapping semantic support, and citation-preserving replacement. A replacement must contain the complete source spans of the original hit, preserve order or shortlist membership as specified and fit 512 tokens. Test a second structural layout under identical rules to expose gains from extra text or different boundaries alone.
validation: Report independently frozen structural, pure semantic, union, second-structural and coverage-preserving nominees on previous confirmation, replication, shared replication, and a new disjoint holdout of 24 stories, 24 research papers and 10 meetings, both source-known and shared. Report domain-balanced coverage, first-hit citation F1, token length, index cost and paired source bootstrap intervals. To call semantic unequivocally better, require positive first- and five-hit deltas versus retuned blocks in both holdout pools, paired lower 95% bounds above zero there, and no material loss of focus or return-size control. Reordering identical top fives can preserve but cannot increase their coverage.
